cases.task_question: How many concurrent writers does SQLite support?

evidence_points.text: Number of writers SQLite allows at the same time
Effect of WAL mode on readers and writers

rows.title: Write-Ahead Logging
rows.content: WAL provides more concurrency as readers do not block writers and a writer does not block readers. However, there can only be one writer at a time.
rows.raw_content: Write-Ahead Logging. WAL provides more concurrency as readers do not block writers and a writer does not block readers. Reading and writing can proceed concurrently. However, since there is only one WAL file, there can only be one writer at a time.
rows.label: relevant

rows.title: File Locking And Concurrency In SQLite Version 3
rows.content: An EXCLUSIVE lock is needed in order to write to the database file. Only one EXCLUSIVE lock is allowed on the file.
rows.raw_content: File Locking And Concurrency In SQLite Version 3. An EXCLUSIVE lock is needed in order to write to the database file. Only one EXCLUSIVE lock is allowed on the file and no other locks of any kind are allowed to coexist with an EXCLUSIVE lock.
rows.label: relevant

rows.title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
rows.content: The 403 (Forbidden) status code indicates that the server understood the request but refuses to fulfill it.
rows.raw_content: 15.5.4. 403 Forbidden. The 403 (Forbidden) status code indicates that the server understood the request but refuses to fulfill it. A server that wishes to make public why the request has been forbidden can describe that reason in the response content.
